sources.citation: OLAC: resources in and about the Guya language (language-archives.org, up to date 2025-11-03; Internet Archive copy)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: three items (Glottolog, Ethnologue, LINGUIST List). No primary texts, lexicon or description in any OLAC archive.

sources.citation: Carter, John, Katie Carter, John Grummitt, Bonnie MacKenzie & Janell Masters. 2012. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Mur Village Vernaculars. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2012-043. Dallas: SIL International. 90 pp.
sources.note: Wordlist-type survey of the Mur (Degenan) area with Warup-family comparison lists (Glottolog language code: Forak, Muratayak, Degenan, Gwahatike.; Guya not listed). Low chance of a Guya statement; listed only because it is the other modern Warup-area report and sil.org was unreachable (not reachable by automated download) so it could not be checked.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province. Pacific Linguistics D-30.
sources.note: Guya/Guiarak does not occur in the volume (the Finisterre languages are outside its Rai Coast stock scope).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. 187 pp. (ANU hdl 1885/146580)
sources.note: Irrelevant to Guya: covers Western Madang (Adelbert Range) languages; 'Guiarak', 'Warup' and 'Finisterre' do not occur in the text.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid guya1251 and Warup family waru1269 reference tables (17 refs for the family)
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Guya: 4 refs, none descriptive (Z'graggen 1975, Ethnologue 16, WOLP, LL-MAP). Warup family: the only descriptions are for Gwahatike [dah] (An & An 1993 Grammar Essentials ms; Gawak kep dictionary 1999) plus SIL surveys of Degenan/Forak/Muratayak/Tanda and the Mur village survey (Carter et al. 2012, SIL ESR 2012-043, language code list does not include Guya).

sources.citation: SIL OAI harvest dump (local, searched for subject gka / Guiarak / Guya / Guyarak
sources.note: No SIL record at all carries Guya as a subject language; the only hit is the 2023 Warup survey via its title.

sources.citation: Carter, John, Devin O'Bannon, Beautlyn Eliab, Karl Kama, Roger Maikei & Napa Yanderave. 2023. Survey Report for Uma (Ronji) [roe], Tandɨ (Yagomi) [ygm], Muratayak [asx], Degenang (Degenan) [dge], and Forak [frq] Languages. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2023-003. SIL International. 71 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Guya is mentioned once, §1.2.6 p.11, repeating Z'graggen's 1975 placement of 'Guiarak (Guya) [gka]' in the Warup family; Guya itself was not surveyed, no wordlist, no phonological notes; 'stress'/'accent'/'tone' absent from the report.

sources.citation: Moe, Jonathan. 2021. A Phonology of the Domung [dev] Language. MA thesis, Trinity Western University. 119 pp. (Finisterre accent survey, Tables 29-30)
sources.note: Its survey of accent across Finisterre languages represents the Warup family by Gwahatike [dah] only (An & An 1990; Price n.d.: 'Accent typically falls on the first syllable; if the word is trisyllabic, it moves to the second syllable if it is a long vowel'). Guya is not included; confirms no phonological description of Guya was known to SIL-PNG as of 2021.

sources.citation: Ethnologue 22nd ed. (2019), entry 'Guya' (Internet Archive copy; ethnologue.com could not be reached by automated download here)
sources.note: Nothing linguistic: pop. 130 (Wurm & Hattori 1981), 20 km west of Seure, Warup, no dialects, 'Guiarak is a village name'.

In Nicholas Evans & Marian Klamer (eds.), Melanesian Languages on the Edge of Asia: Challenges for the 21st Century (Language Documentation & Conservation Special Publication 5), 13-33, with appendix '' (per-language source list). sources.note: Nothing; it is a coverage bibliography.e. no wordlist, sketch or phonology existed then, matching Glottolog 5.3 today.

sources.citation: Suter, Edgar. 1997. A comparative look at the dual and plural forms of verb inflections and pronouns in Northeast New Guinea Papuan languages. Language and Linguistics in Melanesia 28: 17-68.
sources.note: Nothing on stress, tone or accent for any language (0 matches in 28 scanned pages); the paper is about dual/plural consonant alternations in pronouns and verb endings plus supporting cognate sets. Its Guya content is one bracketed form [malj] 'shoot' (scanned rendering; probably [malʸ] or similar in the print).

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1975. North-Eastern Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 527-567. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. §2.8.1.3.7.3 'Guiarak (WR-49), pop. 130. Warup Census Division: Daban, Guiarak, and Kabumdangin.' (p.540); Warup family section credits Claassen with 'noting' Guiarak; no phonological data and no stress/accent/tone remark anywhere in the chapter.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU. 154 pp. (ANU Open Research hdl 1885/146484, CC BY-SA 4.0)
sources.note: Nothing. Guya appears only as 'A13 Guiarak' (pop. 131: Daban 41, Guiarak 76, Kabumdanging 14) in the Warup Family village/population lists (p.17; census table p.48). No wordlist, no phonology; the words 'stress', 'accent', 'tone' do not occur in the volume.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1973. Towards a typology of the Finisterre-Huon languages, New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-22. Canberra: ANU.
sources.harvard_location: Divinity School Library (offsite storage), call number - Ask at Circulation (Pamph. folio) BS 354 .Z91
sources.note: Guya/Guiarak not among the languages covered (Warup family listed as Degenan, Asat, Morafa, Dahating only); nothing on Guya.

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11, Pacific Linguistics A-23: 45-78. Canberra: ANU. (ANU Open Research hdl 1885/254286)
sources.note: Nothing about Guya. §2.2.1 (p.53, p.8): 'Informants stated that the people of Monara and Guiarak villages speak either a divergent dialect of Asat or a different language.' No Guiarak data collected; the paper's phoneme notes concern Suroi, Rawa, Wantoat etc; no stress statement for any language.

sources.note: Closest described relative (Warup family, Gwahatike/Dahating). Would only give a family-level comparandum (initial accent per Moe 2021's summary), not a Guya statement; Glottolog marks the PDF 'nosharefn'.

sources.citation: Any unpublished SIL-PNG or Pioneer Bible Translators field notes / wordlists from the 1995 joint survey of the Asat (Muratayak), Forak and Asaro'o areas, or later Warup-area survey work that may have elicited Guiarak village data (referred to in Carter et al. 2023 §1.2.6)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The 2023 survey cites a 1995 SIL-PNG/PBT survey of the neighbouring Warup languages; it is the only fieldwork in the immediate area since 1970 and the only conceivable place a Guiarak wordlist with stress marks might sit. Not located in the SIL OAI dump; probably unpublished.
